model_annotation: The plot titled “23.9 M, Nanodo, C4” illustrates how two normalized sharpness-composition traces evolve over training. The x-axis is labeled “Training Steps,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 6400 with regularly spaced tick labels at 0, 1600, 3200, 4800, and 6400. The y-axis is labeled “Sharpness composition,” uses a logarithmic scale, and shows labeled ticks at \(10^{0}\), \(10^{-1}\), \(10^{-2}\), and \(10^{-3}\). Two solid lines are shown with no visible markers: a blue line that stays near \(10^{0}\) throughout (starting around \(\sim 1.0\) at step 0 and remaining close to \(\sim 1.0\) by step 6400 with small undulations), and an orange line that begins near \(\sim 10^{0}\) at step 0, drops sharply within the early steps to around \(\sim 10^{-2}\) (near its lowest point shortly after the start), then rises and fluctuates mostly between roughly \(\sim 2\times 10^{-2}\) and \(\sim 5\times 10^{-2}\) for much of the mid-range, includes a noticeable spike reaching just under \(10^{-1}\) around the mid-to-late portion of training (approximately in the 3200–3600 step region), and then tapers back down toward the end, finishing near \(\sim 2\times 10^{-2}\) by step 6400.
